transcript:
Meeting Header: 2025-11-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM); Marta, Evan, Samir (CedarLane)

Summary: Quick intros, then deep dive on what counts as PII, how CedarLane wants prompts stored (never, ephemeral, or encrypted), retention TTLs per environment, and sizing for the POC. Benchmarks agreed: cold start, steady-state, and burst (200 qps) runs; measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost.

00:00 Jordan: All right, hey everybody, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan from Redwood — I'm the AE on this — quick intros, then Priya will jump in on the technical plan.
00:18 Marta: Hey Jordan, Marta here, head of ML at CedarLane. Appreciate it.
00:22 Evan: Evan, security architect.
00:24 Samir: Samir, platform eng.
00:27 Priya: Priya, SE at Redwood. We'll aim to keep this practical.
00:31 Jordan: Goal for today is to lock success criteria and scope the POC. We got your initial note about PII and retention.
00:41 Marta: Yep. High level — we need to prove two things: first, that Redwood can redact or prevent storage of PII from prompts and logs; second, that we can hit latency targets at our expected load without exploding cost.
00:55 Priya: Great. Can you share the expected traffic profile? QPS, average tokens per request?
01:03 Samir: Right now the app sees around 30 QPS baseline, peaks up to ~200 for short bursts, average prompt is ~420 tokens including system messages, responses average 180 tokens.
01:18 Jordan: Cool. So for sizing we should test baseline 30 qps steady-state, and a 200 qps 5-minute burst. We'll aim for p95 < 350ms on the simple completions and p99 under 800ms for typical prompts — is that realistic for you?
01:34 Marta: For user-facing flows p95 < 350ms is preferable; p99 we can tolerate up to 900ms if it's rare. Cost target would be roughly $X per 1M tokens — we'll discuss later.
01:45 Evan: Security side — we need to ensure the prompts that contain end-user PII are not retained unencrypted or logged in plain text. We have to show how Redwood handles PII redaction, prompt storage TTLs by environment, and key management.
01:58 Priya: Understood. On PII redaction we support two levers: 1) streaming redaction where we run a pre-processing redactor in-line (customer-provided regex/PII model) and 2) platform-side redaction — configurable retention TTLs and prompt redaction rules. Note: platform-side redaction can be tuned but we recommend you run an initial local sanitizer to avoid edge cases.
02:20 Samir: If platform-side redaction is used, how auditable is that? We need to prove removal for compliance.
02:27 Priya: We emit audit logs with redaction events. The retention TTL governs how long the raw prompt is held; after TTL we replace with redacted artifact. Audit logs show the before/after hash and the redaction rule applied. The export shows timestamps but we can mask actual PII in exports.
02:41 Evan: Is the audit log itself containing raw prompts? That's a no for us.
02:45 Priya: Audit logs do not store raw PII by default — they store metadata and hashes. Full raw prompt is held only in a protected store until TTL expiry if you opt-in. For the POC we can set TTL to zero for raw prompts (no storage) and just keep redaction metadata.
02:59 Marta: That sounds promising. We still need to validate the redaction accuracy with our data — we'll send a ~2000-row sample with annotated PII.
03:08 Jordan: Perfect. We'll treat that as the canonical test set.
03:12 Priya: For benchmarks, recommended plan: 1) cold start single instance test, 2) steady-state baseline at 30 qps for 30 minutes, 3) burst 200 qps for 5 minutes. We'll run each scenario three times and report p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and cost numbers.
03:30 Samir: Do you support per-route config for retention? We want different retention TTLs for dev/stage/prod.
03:36 Priya: Yes — retention is per-route. You can tag routes with TTLs and override at request level via headers.
03:44 Evan: KMS — we plan to use an HSM-backed KMS. Does Redwood integrate with external KMS or only cloud KMS?
03:52 Priya: We support customer KMS via standard integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys via partner integrations. For Private deployments we can support an on-prem HSM. We'll need the exact KMS flow and policy document for the security review.
04:06 Jordan: Action: Evan to send KMS requirements, Priya will validate compatibility.
04:11 Evan: Noted.
04:13 Jordan: On deployment modes — for the POC would you prefer hosted for speed or dedicated/private?
04:18 Marta: We want to start hosted to move fast but we may need dedicated if latency/cost requirements aren't met. Also legal may require private for production later.
04:27 Priya: Agreed. Hosted for initial runs; if metrics miss targets we'll re-evaluate dedicated or Private (VPC). For the POC we can simulate dedicated load profiles on our hosted infra to get realistic numbers.
04:40 Samir: How are caches handled? We need to ensure KV-cache or prefix cache doesn't leak PII between tenants.
04:47 Priya: Cache is tenant-isolated; KV cache entries are namespaced per customer. However, caching of prompts is configurable. For PII we recommend disabling prompt caching and only using short-lived KV cache for model state.
04:59 Marta: Ok. Regarding prompt storage: we want options of 1) never store raw prompts, 2) store encrypted for X days, 3) store redacted only. Can you support all three?
05:10 Priya: Yes. Those are supported. For 1) you'd set TTL=0 and no retention; for 2) TTL >0 with customer KMS; for 3) enable platform redaction pipeline and store only redacted artifacts. We'll document the request headers and per-route flags.
05:25 Jordan: Let's talk success criteria concretely — Marta?
05:29 Marta: Acceptance: redaction precision > 99% on our annotated set, p95 latency < 350ms for primary route, and cost under our defined threshold (we'll give a target number). Also stability during 200 qps bursts with no errors > 0.1%.
05:51 Priya: Noted. We'll map those to pass/fail for the POC. For redaction precision we will run your annotated sample and report false negatives/positives. For latency & errors we'll use our telemetry and instrument route-level alarms.
06:05 Samir: About cost measurement — will you provide an estimated delta for quantization or smaller model variants? We might trade quality for cost.
06:13 Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching profiles. For the POC we'll test the same model at FP16 and an 8-bit quantized variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll flag any observable quality regressions against your reference prompts.
06:28 Marta: That helps. For benchmarks, do you run model compilation per hardware profile? We have two target regions with different GPU types.
06:36 Priya: We do per-hardware kernel selection. For hosted we'll run on the GPU family that most closely matches your prod target; we'll document the exact instance type. If you want dedicated we can reserve specific GPU types.
06:46 Jordan: Quick note — legal asked about eDiscovery for audit: can we export redaction events and prove deletion?
06:52 Priya: Yes — we can export an audit package with timestamps and hashes showing deletion. The raw content won't be included if TTL hit zero at deletion time.
06:59 Evan: What about retention windows per user vs per route? We have to handle compliance requests to delete a specific user's data.
07:07 Priya: You can issue a user-delete operation, and the platform will remove entries associated with that user across the prompt store and replace with redacted placeholder; audit log records the deletion event. We'll demonstrate this in the POC.
07:19 Samir: Network egress — for Private we need a checklist: firewall rules, peering, etc. If we move to Private, we need a preflight.
07:27 Jordan: We'll schedule a preflight network checklist call with infra. Action: Jordan to coordinate if Private goes ahead.
07:33 Marta: Timeline: We're targeting a 6-8 week POC, with pilot demo in week 4 and final report in week 8. Is that feasible?
07:41 Priya: Yes. Week 0: kickoff and data handover; week 1-2: benchmark runs & redaction tuning; week 3-4: repeat benchmarks and run stochastic tests; week 5: security review and interim demo; week 6-8: follow-up tuning and final report.
07:58 Jordan: We'll draft a timeline and post it in the shared doc.
08:02 Marta: For the sample data, how do you want it delivered? Anonymized CSV + labels?
08:07 Priya: Anonymized CSV with annotations for PII types is ideal. If you can provide a small set of raw examples under an NDA for internal redaction model tuning that helps; otherwise we'll work with the anonymized set.
08:19 Evan: We'll need an NDA supplement for sample raw data; legal will push that through.
08:23 Jordan: Fine. We'll wait for that.
08:26 Samir: A question on telemetry retention — what part of the telemetry contains prompt snippets? We want to avoid even short snippets in logs.
08:34 Priya: Telemetry defaults to metrics+traces with no raw prompts. Only full debug logs include snippet fields and those are gated behind an opt-in and TTL. For POC we'll keep debug disabled and extract metrics only.
08:46 Marta: Great. I want to test false-positive redaction (i.e., removing non-PII)—do you have a way to tune the redactor?
08:52 Priya: Yes. The redactor engine supports rule whitelists and confidence thresholds; we can tune to reduce false positives. We'll run a tuning pass with your annotations and produce a precision/recall matrix.
09:04 Jordan: Ok next topic — dataset size for the POC: you mentioned 2k rows for redaction validation, but for throughput tests we need realistic arrival patterns. Samir, you said 30 qps baseline — any diurnal patterns?
09:17 Samir: Peak hours are 11am–2pm local where you'll see 60 qps sustained for an hour; otherwise small bursts. We'll feed a synthetic traffic file reflecting that.
09:26 Priya: Good — send a 24hr synthetic traffic profile CSV and we'll use it to drive the load generator.
09:31 Marta: We'll do that.
09:33 Jordan: A couple of gotchas — third-party log sinks. Are you sending request payloads to Splunk? If so we need to scrub at the source.
09:40 Evan: We do ship logs to Splunk. We'll change the pipeline to avoid raw prompts being shipped.
09:45 Priya: Also note that model outputs should be scanned for accidental leakage of PII and we can run an out-bound redaction check on responses too.
09:54 Marta: That's important. We want both in-bound and out-bound redaction checks.
09:57 Priya: We'll include response scanning in the benchmark plan.
10:01 Jordan: On success criteria again — what constitutes failure? Marta?
10:06 Marta: If redaction precision <98% on the annotated set, or p95 latency exceeds 500ms consistently, or error rates >0.5% during burst tests — we'd call it a miss. There's some wiggle room for early tuning.
10:21 Priya: Understood. We'll flag those thresholds in the POC report and mark which tests are pass/fail.
10:27 Samir: Can you share the measurement tooling? We need to map their metrics to our observability stack for parity.
10:34 Priya: We'll share Grafana dashboards and raw metric exports (Prometheus) for the test runs. We'll also provide an S3 export of raw telemetry for offline analysis if needed.
10:44 Jordan: Competitors — Marta, you mentioned some internal evaluations of Anthropic and openAI — any specific gaps you saw there?
10:51 Marta: Main issue was cost at scale and lack of per-route retention controls, plus their redaction tooling was more manual. Also we wanted deterministic rollbacks for model versions.
11:02 Priya: Redwood's rollouts support canary and A/B and automatic fallback to a cheaper but compatible model variant; we'll demo that in the pilot.
11:11 Samir: On the pilot model — what model do you recommend for CedarLane's use case?
11:15 Priya: For banking style content we recommend a mid-sized open model with strong instruction tuning — we'll propose two variants: one for quality (bigger model) and one quantized for cost. We'll test both.
11:27 Marta: Fine. Please call out if hallucination rates change with quantization.
11:32 Priya: Will do — we'll calculate a QA score vs your reference outputs.
11:36 Jordan: Logistics — where will we store the benchmark artifacts and results?
11:39 Priya: We'll create a shared drive link and push the benchmark spreadsheet, timelines, and demo recording. Links: POC plan doc: [link-to-doc], benchmark sheet: [link-to-sheet].
11:51 Marta: Great.
11:53 Evan: One more security ask — we need to run a short penetration test against the endpoint for the POC. Would Redwood allow that?
11:59 Priya: Yes, controlled pentest allowed under our policy. We'll need scope & schedule and a signed attestation. I'll send the policy doc.
12:09 Jordan: Anything else?
12:11 Marta: Not from me. Looking forward to the pricing so we can budget.
12:14 Jordan: Action recap: Jordan shares pricing and infra diagram; Priya runs micro-benchmarks & shares plan; Marta sends annotated samples and traffic profile; Evan sends KMS reqs; we aim to kick off next Monday pending NDA and sample data.
12:30 Lena: I'll set up the calendar invite and the shared drive.
12:34 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOW.
12:37 Marta: Thanks all.

Artifacts referenced: POC plan doc (link-to-doc), Benchmark spreadsheet (link-to-sheet), Redwood redaction policy (link-to-policy), KMS integration checklist (link-to-checklist).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., "sock two" for SOC2, "K-V cash" for KV cache) — corrected in summary. Speaker overlap present around 08:00–09:00.

End of transcript.
